To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neonatal rabbits exposed to the P-450-activating toxicant, 4-ipomeolan, have a reduced expression of the differentiation markers of Clara cells and a reduced number of ciliated cells in their bronchioles compared to control neonatal rabbits.
neonatal rabbits treated with 4-ipomeanl on day 7 develop squamous metaplasia of the bronchiole and a loss of Clara cell differentiation.

4-ipomeanl, at a dose that is 100-fold lower than that required to injure adult rabbit Clara cells, alters bronchiolar epithelia in neonates, and the alterations are most severe when injury occurs during the period of differentiation of Clara cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Clara cells in lung development, their differentiation, and their role in the response to environmental toxicants.
the mechanisms of injury and repair of bronchiolar epithelia.
the role of Clara cells in the pathogenesis of lung injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
early injury to developing Clara cells by 4-ipomeneal alters bronchiolar epithelia of adult rabbits.
the bronchioles of 4-ipomonal treated animals are lined with squamous epithelial cell zones, and that these zones are the result of the injury and repair of neonatal Clara cells.
early injury to developing bronchiolar epithelia by a cytochromep-450-dependent cytotoxicant inhibits bronchial epithelial differentiation and alters repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Clara cell differentiation is an extremely sensitive process that is susceptible to injury by a variety of environmental toxicants and that the resulting damage to the epithelium may have a significant impact on bronchiolar function.
4-ipomeanal, at low doses, causes injury to the differentiating neonatal Clara cell and, at higher doses, injury to the mature Clara cell.
the bronchiolar Clara cells of the developing rabbit are more sensitive to injury by 4-ip-omeanol than those of the adult.
The main takeaway from our work is that

early exposure to a toxicant that injures the bronchiole may alter the epithelial organization of the adult bronchiole, and that the impact of the injury may be more profound in the neonate than in the adult.
the bronchiolar organization of adult rabbits can be dramatically affected by early injury to differenti-ating Clara cells.
the bronchiolar airway epithelium is a dynamic structure, and injury to this tissue during early development may lead to long-term changes in the epithelium.
